title: In vitro induction of trained immunity in adherent human monocytes
protocol: Heat PBS at 37°C.
Prepare RPMI+ by adding Glutamax, pyruvate, and gentamicin to complete RPMI 1640 medium.
Warm RPMI+ at 37°C.
Suspend monocytes at a concentration of 10^6 cells/ml in RPMI+.
Add 100 μL of cell suspension per well in a sterile 96-well clear flat bottom polystyrene tissue culture-treated plate.
Incubate the plate for 1 hour at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Remove supernatant containing non-adherent cells after incubation.
Wash remaining non-adherent cells by adding and discarding 200 μL of warm PBS per well.
Add 200 μL of corresponding trained immunity-inducing stimuli in warm RPMI+ supplemented with 10% human pooled serum per well.
Use RPMI+ as a negative control.
Use 1 μg/ml β-glucan or 5 μg/ml BCG as positive controls.
Incubate 24 hours at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Try the protocol with different concentrations of serum (0%–10%) for each new stimulus tested.
Compare percentages of apoptosis/cell death in wells treated with different serum concentrations over time.
Use PBS containing calcium for all steps to prevent cell detachment.
Discard supernatant or use it for cytokine measurement and/or LDH cytotoxicity assay on day 1.
Wash off remaining stimuli with 200 μL warm PBS without EDTA.
Add 200 μL warm RPMI+ supplemented with 10% pooled human serum.
Incubate for 6 days, refreshing the medium once at day 3.
Discard supernatant or use it for cytokine measurement and/or LDH cytotoxicity assay on day 3.
Add 200 μL warm RPMI+ supplemented with 10% pooled human serum.
Discard supernatant or use for cytokine measurement and/or LDH cytotoxicity assay.
Add 200 μL of warm RPMI+ with a secondary stimulus.
Incubate for 24 h at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Centrifuge the plates at 350 × g for 8 min.
Collect 180 μL of supernatants.
Use collected supernatants immediately or freeze them at −20°C for assessment within 2 to 4 weeks, or at −80°C for further assessment.
Count live cells with trypan blue by diluting the cells 1:5 with Trypan Blue and counting non-stained cells in a hemocytometer.
Normalize cytokine production per cell number if the numbers of cells differ.
Perform LDH cytotoxicity assay with fresh supernatants following manufacturer instructions.
Include a positive control for cell lysis in the LDH assay.
Include a negative control (medium only) in the LDH assay.
Assess cytokine levels by ELISA on Day 7 or later.
Follow manufacturer's instructions for performing ELISA.
Dilute samples if cytokine concentrations are above detection limits of commercial kits.
Optimize dilution range based on stimulus, laboratory conditions, and donor variability.
Use R&D Duoset ELISA kits with specific dilution ranges as specified.
